name: Manaslu Expedition
sub_region: Gorkha District (Samagaon, Chumnubri Rural Municipality), Gandaki Province

difficulty.notes: Eighth-highest mountain; Northeast Face normal route with four camps above base camp. Considered a comparatively 'achievable' 8,000 m peak but with ice cliffs below Camp 4, avalanche-prone slopes and an exposed, corniced final ridge to the true summit. [s5, s9]

duration_days.notes: Most operators fly by helicopter to Samagaon and walk out to Soti Khola/Machha Khola; others trek in via the Budhi Gandaki or over Larkya La from Dharapani (36 days). [s5, s6, s7]

start_point: Kathmandu (helicopter to Samagaon, or overland via Machha Khola / Dharapani)

itinerary.route: Arrival in Kathmandu; briefing, gear check, permits

itinerary.notes: Some operators trek in over approx. 8 days instead. [s5]

itinerary.route: Puja and acclimatization rotations to Camp 1 (approx. 5,500-5,700 m), Camp 2 (approx. 6,250-6,400 m) and Camp 3 (approx. 6,800 m)
itinerary.notes: Camp altitudes vary by operator. [s5, s9]

itinerary.route: Summit window: Camp 4 (approx. 7,400-7,450 m) and summit, descend to Base Camp
Descend to Samagaon, trek out to Soti Khola (or helicopter) and drive to Kathmandu

best_seasons.notes: Manaslu is Nepal's busiest autumn 8,000 m peak: DoT reported 500 permits from 43 teams in autumn 2026 (earlier counts 480 and 493). In 2026 the rope-fixing team reached the true summit on 17 Sept, but persistent rain and snow led operators to close the Manaslu season around 22 Sept. [s10, s11, s12]

permits.name: Department of Tourism climbing royalty - Mt. Manaslu
permits.fee: Foreign climber per person: USD 1,500 spring, USD 3,000 autumn, USD 1,500 winter/summer

permits.name: Garbage management deposit (refundable, per team) - peaks above 8,000 m other than Everest
Manaslu Restricted Area trekking permit
permits.fee: Must be obtained, but Department of Immigration states expedition-permit holders do not pay the trekking permit fee for restricted areas (standard RAP: Sep-Nov USD 100/week + USD 15/day; Dec-Aug USD 75/week + USD 10/day)

permits.name: Government liaison officer
permits.fee: Operators quote about USD 2,000 per team; no official rate found

guide_requirements: Mountaineering Regulation sixth amendment (in force 1 Sept 2025): no solo expeditions on 8,000 m peaks; every two members must be accompanied by at least one high-altitude worker or mountain guide. Mandatory accident insurance minimums: NPR 2 million for mountain guides and high-altitude workers, NPR 1.5 million for liaison officers and base camp workers, NPR 500,000 for local workers, plus medical insurance for staff. [s2, s3]

flights: Helicopter Kathmandu - Samagaon (common on commercial expeditions)
Samagaon - Base Camp helicopter approx. 15-20 minutes air time, weather permitting
drives: Machha Khola/Soti Khola - Kathmandu by road (walk-out)
Kathmandu - Besisahar - Dharapani (Larkya La approach variant)
logistics.notes: Lodges in Samagaon; tented base camp and high camps. The 11 Oct 2026 Budhi Gandaki flood destroyed the lower trail between Jagat and Philim, affecting overland walk-outs. [s5, s8, s15]

highlights: Classic Northeast Face route with four camps
Often a first 8,000 m peak and Everest preparation
risks: Avalanche (e.g. an avalanche above Camp 3 disrupted rope fixing on 16 Sept 2026)
Exposed, corniced final ridge to the true summit (fore-summit vs true summit issue)
Weather closures (autumn 2026 season closed early by snowfall)

acclimatization.notes: Several days at Samagaon and base camp, then rotations through the camps before the summit window. [s5]

unverified: Liaison officer fee (USD 2,000 per team) comes from a single operator.
High camp altitudes vary between operators (Camp 1 5,500-5,700 m; Camp 2 6,250-6,400 m; Camp 4 7,400-7,450 m).
Final autumn 2026 Manaslu permit count reported variously as 480, 493 and 500.
